newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks amble to lower close.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks amble to lower close.

text.p: 10yrbond futs 92.430 -0.160 Gold NY 368.25 Lon fix 368.25
*Stocks end lower, drop in Dow depresses and National Aust Bank ex-div weighs on market. Volume 432.7 million, value A$1.19 bln, 1,076 stocks traded, 326 steady, 300 up, 450 down
Australian shares ambled to a lower close on Tuesday after a drop in the Dow depressed sentiment and a crumbling copper price impacted on BHP.
Also weighing on the market was National Australia Bank which went ex-dividend its final payout of 44 cents.
At 4.10 p.m. (0510 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 20.5 points lower at 2,315.8. December share index futures were 20 points lower at 2,313, a 2.8 point discount to the index.
Active trade in National Australia Bank shares belied a day of otherwise moderate turnover with even less action.
With the share prices of the market's two largest companies, BHP and National Australia Bank, heading south it would have taken a herculean effort to avoid today's losses.
Between them, BHP and National Australia Bank account for over 16 percent of the benchmark All Ordinaries index.

"It was generally weaker but NAB (National Australia Bank) and Hills (BHP) were the big losers today," said a Sydney-based dealer, adding that the resource sector was bearing the brunt of softer base metals prices in offshore markets.
"The miners took most of it after metals fell but the Dow gave us no joy anyway," he said.
"That copper price was hit pretty hard overnight as were other commodity prices, so it was no surprise to see commodity stocks down today," said dealer Hamish Dee of Brisbane brokerage Lance Jones.
Dee said he was expecting little to eventuate from a meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve, due later today.
"I think the expectation is for them to keep rates steady. Most people are looking at well into 1997 before any change there."
National Australia Bank trade dominated proceedings with over A$441 million worth of its scrip traded.

Catching trader's attention early was technology group, Zylotech, whose shares surged after it announced the international release of its FILMLINK technology which allows high quality video to be streamed live over computer networks.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of three to two, while about 30 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures trade was moderate, although options activity was substantially slower in line with the underlying markets.
Total options traded 31,880 (50,564)
Turnover in December SPI contracts totalled 7,706 (5,553)

In other local markets, some late selling into a thin market saw Australian bonds finish Tuesday near their lows and well down on their previous closes, traders said. By 5.15 p.m. (0615 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.50 percent.

The Australian dollar tested the bounds of its recent tight range but the feeble flailing failed to stir the market from its year-end slumber. The price action, which had more to do with a patchy market than meaningful flows, confirmed the resilience of the US$0.7910-0.7950 range which has dominated since the unit crumbled from atop 80 cents last week. By 5.00 pm (0600 GMT), the unit was at US$0.7935/40 from US$0.7930/35 late Monday.
